title: 〜を限りに
meaning: as of …, no more; from … on (something ends); with all one's …
simpleExplanation: 〜を限りに marks a point after which something stops: 今日を限りにタバコをやめる (as of today, I quit smoking), 今月末を限りに閉店 (closing at the end of this month). 限り = "limit", so the time word is the last day. A second use, 声を限りに / 力の限り, means "with all one's voice / strength".
whenUsed: Formal announcements, resolutions and business notices (closures, retirements, ends of service). The first use always expresses an ending, never a beginning. The second use is literary (声を限りに叫ぶ).
formation: N(time / event) + を限りに + ending (やめる・閉店する・引退する・終了する)
声を限りに / 力の限り (with all one's voice / strength)
Set: 本日を限りに・今回を限りに

examples.ja: 今日を限りに、タバコをやめることにした。
examples.reading: きょうをかぎりに、タバコをやめることにした。
examples.en: As of today, I have decided to quit smoking.
examples.note: A personal resolution: today is the last day of smoking.

examples.ja: 当店は今月末を限りに閉店いたします。
examples.reading: とうてんはこんげつまつをかぎりにへいてんいたします。
examples.en: This shop will close at the end of this month.
examples.note: A shop closure notice: 今月末を限りに閉店.

examples.ja: 子供たちは声を限りに応援した。
examples.reading: こどもたちはこえをかぎりにおうえんした。
examples.en: The children cheered at the top of their voices.
examples.note: The literary use: 声を限りに = with all their voice.

examples.ja: この試合を限りに、彼は現役を引退すると発表した。
examples.reading: このしあいをかぎりに、かれはげんえきをいんたいするとはっぴょうした。
examples.en: He announced that he would retire from active play after this match.
examples.note: An event, not only a date, can be the limit.

examples.ja: 今回を限りに、こうした特別対応は行いません。
examples.reading: こんかいをかぎりに、こうしたとくべつたいおうはおこないません。
examples.en: This will be the last time we make such a special arrangement.
examples.note: Business notice: no more exceptions after this one.

similarGrammar.difference: A formal cutoff point that can start or end something (本日をもって開始). を限りに only ends.
Marks the first of a series that continues: the opposite direction.
"Since X": a starting point with continuation up to now, not an ending.

commonMistakes.wrong: 今日を限りに、ジョギングを始める。
commonMistakes.right: 今日から、ジョギングを始める。
commonMistakes.why: を限りに marks an end; for a start use から or をもって.

commonMistakes.right: 今日を限りに、やめます。／今日限りで、やめます。
commonMistakes.why: The pattern needs を; the alternative is 今日限りで.

commonMistakes.wrong: 十時を限りに閉店します。（毎日の営業時間）
commonMistakes.why: Daily closing times are simple facts; を限りに is for a permanent end.

usageNotes: The predicate is nearly always a verb of stopping or ending: やめる・引退する・閉店する・終了する・打ち切る.
本日を限りに / 今回を限りに are the most frequent forms in notices.
声を限りに and 力の限り are separate idioms meaning "to the limit of"; do not mix them with the time use.
jlptTips: A date or event + blank + an ending verb → を限りに.
The main distractor is をもって; if the sentence could also mean "start", をもって is more likely, and if the verb is やめる / 引退する, を限りに is the natural key.
In 並べ替え, keep N + を限りに together and place the ending verb after it.
